newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Convicted Cavallo warns enemies he's a "fighter".
newsitem.headline: Convicted Cavallo warns enemies he's a "fighter".

text.p: Argentina's battling former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo, given a four-month suspended jail term for slander and facing over 20 more suits, warned his many enemies Wednesday that he was a "fighter."

The first legal setback for the free-market zealout's campaign against alleged corruption in the Peronist government and in the courts came three days after the first anniversary of his sacking by President Carlos Menem.

Mobbed by reporters outside his home, Cavallo said Tuesday night's verdict in a slander suit by a former customs official was a warning "for the future of the country and the people in general." He scheduled a news conference for later Wednesday.
"I am a fighter, and fights are tough," he said.

Between 1991 and 1995, Cavallo engineered Argentina's emergence from economic chaos to a zero-inflation economy. But he angered Menem with his constant corruption charges, and is held responsible by many for unemployment of 16.1 percent.
Opposition leaders with no love for Cavallo condemned the verdict. Graciela Fernandez Meijide of the center-left Frepaso said it looked "suspiciously like political revenge."
The sentence was handed down by Federal Judge Rodolfo Canicoba in the first of more than 20 suits pending against Cavallo, many by officials and judges he has called corrupt.
"This is the first in a long series," said Jorge Matzkin, Peronist leader in the lower house of Congress.

Lawyer Jorge Kolon, suing Cavallo for corruption charges dating back to 1992 which he says got him fired from his job in the customs office and prevented him being named judge, said Tuesday night he was "satisfied justice has been done."
The sentence fell short of the plaintiff's demand for a one-year prison term and that Cavallo be sent on a human rights course and be banned from holding public office for a year.
Had Kolon got his way, Cavallo would have had to withdraw his candidacy for a seat in Congress in October's mid-term elections for his newly-formed party Action for the Republic.

"I will not be thrown out of the political field so easily," Cavallo said before Tuesday's verdict, adding that he felt "politically persecuted" by judges he alleges are in the pockets of his arch-enemy Interior Minister Carlos Corach.
Since being sacked, Cavallo has accused Menem and cabinet ministers of being in the control of the controversial tycoon Alfredo Yabran, whom he says is the head of a powerful crime ring.

Cavallo, whose bald pate, bright blue eyes and easy tongue make him the favorite butt of cartoonists' jokes, came out of Tuesday's verdict spitting angry and shouting, "Yabran's got him under control, that's what's wrong with Menem."
In early July, Cavallo scored one legal victory whan a suit against him by Yabran was thrown out of court.
